## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pūtimaṁsajātaka* (Ja 437) is a canonical Jātaka tale situated in the *Jātaka* collection of the Pali canon. The text opens with the verse phrase *Na kho me ruccatîti* (“Why thus does Putimansa”) [Fausböll 1883]. According to the narrative framework preserved in V. Fausböll's edition of the Jātaka commentary, the Buddha delivered the discourse while residing at Jetavana, taking occasion from a situation where several monks had failed to guard the doors of their senses (*indriyesu aguttadvārā*), thereby discoursing on the restraint of the senses (*indriyasaṁvara*) [Fausböll 1883]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that in that former life he was the tree spirit (*vanajeṭṭharukkhe nibbattadevatā*) presiding in the principal forest tree [Fausböll 1883].
